ABOUT GEORGIAN

Georgian is a Toronto-based venture capital firm that partners with high-growth technology companies across cybersecurity, AI software, robotics, defense. We manage about $6B in assets and we have invested in more than 80 companies that we support with capital and technical capability.

 

ABOUT THE ROLE

 

As an intern in Georgian’s AI Lab, you’ll work on the brain of the robot: the models it thinks with, the data it learns from, the simulators it practices in and the systems that get all of that onto real machines. You’ll work alongside our scientists and engineers on research, portfolio projects and technical diligence, and you’ll own a scoped project of your own. This is a software role. You won’t design hardware, but you’ll learn enough about the body to understand what it will and won’t let the brain do.

 

WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS

 

Physical AI is a core investment thesis area for us. Our portfolio includes Bedrock Robotics, Path Robotics, Vention, and other frontier robotics companies. We think most of what separates these companies is the brain, not the body: how they collect and use data, the models that see and act, the world models and simulators they train against and the tools that get a new behavior from the lab onto a fleet of machines. That’s the part of the stack you’ll work on as an intern. You’ll help the AI Lab follow the latest in robot learning, run experiments and build tools, and support our work with portfolio companies and on technical diligence. You’ll know how a learned policy behaves on a real robot and what a working sim-to-real pipeline looks like. And you’ll be able to tell a system that’s really deployed from a good demo.

 

WHAT YOU'LL OWN & DELIVER

 

 - Support robot learning research. Help the team keep up with what’s new in VLAs, world models, sim-to-real and evaluation. Reproduce results from recent papers, run experiments and ablation studies, and contribute to internal tech notes and write-ups.

 - Hands-on R&D. Train and evaluate policies in simulation under guidance, using imitation learning or reinforcement learning. Assist in building data pipelines, evaluation setups and small tools that make experiments faster and easier to repeat.

 - Contribute to portfolio projects. Support AI Lab team members working with portfolio companies on robot-learning software. Assist with code implementation, testing and documentation, and help track results the companies care about, like task success rate and how often a person has to step in.

 - Support technical diligence. Help the investment team assess physical AI companies by researching the technical landscape and preparing technical question lists. Document what we find, including whether a company’s autonomy is learned or scripted and how it holds up beyond the demo.

 - Own a scoped project. Take one focused project from idea to result, such as a sim-to-real benchmark, a policy training pipeline or an evaluation of a new model, and present it to the AI Lab and the wider Georgian team.

 - Communicate technical work. Turn what you learn into clear documentation, demos and short presentations for audiences with different technical backgrounds.

 
 

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 

IDEAL ATTRIBUTES

 - Currently pursuing or recently completed a Master’s or PhD in computer science, robotics, electrical engineering or a related field, with a focus on machine learning, reinforcement learning or robotics.

 - Hands-on experience training deep learning models in a modern framework (PyTorch, JAX or similar), with strong Python and clean, reproducible code.

 - Working knowledge of robot learning: imitation learning, reinforcement learning, and the basics of VLAs, world models and sim-to-real transfer.

 - Some exposure to robotics systems through coursework, research, a lab or a competition team, even if you haven’t deployed outside a lab

 - Comfortable with ambiguity and with asking good questions when you’re stuck; a clear writer and speaker

NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Experience with simulators (MuJoCo, Isaac Sim, ManiSkill or similar) or LeRobot

 - Time on real robot hardware, including research, hobby or competition projects

 - Basic C++ and ROS 2, enough to read an on-robot stack

 - Classical robotics background: motion planning, state estimation or control

 - Published work or open-source contributions in robot learning (CoRL, RSS, ICRA, LeRobot or similar)

 - Interest in industries like manufacturing, industrial automation or construction

CULTURAL ATTRIBUTES WE LOVE

 

 - Ambition and agency: You want to do big things and don’t wait to be told; you’re at your best with little structure and a lot of ownership

 - Curiosity: You chase problems to the root cause and keep asking “why,” even when the answer turns out to be a loose cable rather than the model

 - Team over ego: You make the people around you better, colleagues and founders alike

 - Plain talk: You can explain a hard technical thing briefly enough that a busy CEO gets it the first time

 - Builder: You’d rather ship a rough policy to a test cell today than a perfect one next quarter, and you know the difference between a demo and a deployment

 
 

HIRING PROCESS

 

We don't hire like a MAG7 or scale up — in fact we rarely hire compared to them.

 

You shouldn't expect a cookie-cutter high-volume hiring process with us — but a more boutique one that allows you to see a lot of the organization before joining us.

 

We build a thesis in what an individual brings to our very small team, versus simply matching qualifications:

 1. 30‑min intro (values & motivations)

 2. 60‑min technical interview (ML fundamentals & problem‑solving)

 3. Project discussion with team members

 

POSITION STATUS

 

This posting represents an active, future internship vacancy on our team. We are currently interviewing for this role.

OUR COMMITMENT TO ACCESSIBILITY

 Small Print ⇒ We’re looking for a commercially minded lawyer who can protect the business while helping it move forward. Someone who can review an influencer agreement in the morning, research a regulatory question before lunch, and calmly handle a demand letter in the afternoon without sending everyone around them into a panic.
 The good news? AlgaeCal has the world’s only clinically supported natural solution to this problem. We give hope to everyone worried about bone loss. As our Junior Legal Counsel, you’ll help protect that trust. Your work will support responsible growth, compliant innovation, and the ethical decisions that allow us to reach more people without putting our customers, our brands, or our business at unnecessary risk.
 If that excites you, you’ll find no better place to continue your legal career than at AlgaeCal. 
 This job might be for you if you… 
 Have in-house counsel experience. Haven’t got that experience yet? No worries! Articling students and recent law graduates are welcome to apply too.
 Know your way around a contract. You know that the danger in a contract is rarely hiding in the font size. It’s buried in the indemnities, warranties, termination rights, intellectual property provisions, and limitations of liability. You’ve drafted and reviewed commercial agreements before, and you know how to identify the terms that truly matter for the business rather than drafting for academic rigour.
 Understand how business actually works. You don’t practise law in a vacuum. You understand that the goal isn’t simply to eliminate every imaginable risk. It’s to understand the risk, explain the trade-offs, and help the business make a smart decision. You can protect the company without becoming the Department of No. Instead, you’ll work within a team where our approach is How Can I Help. 
 Can make complicated things simple. You can take a complex legal issue and explain it in plain English to someone who has never set foot in law school. You write clear contracts, practical memos, useful summaries, and recommendations that help people understand what they need to do next.
 You know when to push back. You can challenge unreasonable terms without turning every negotiation into a courtroom drama. You know when to stand firm, when to compromise, and when a seemingly small clause creates a much bigger business risk.
 You spot problems early. You naturally notice the legal and compliance issues other people miss. Whether you’re reviewing marketing copy, packaging, a product name, a supplier agreement, or a new business initiative, you know how to identify potential exposure early and recommend a practical way to reduce it.
 You provide solutions. You take the time to understand what another business unit or leader is trying to achieve, uncover the problem behind the request, and bring them a practical solution. You research the options, explain the trade-offs, and set out a clear plan that protects the business while helping everyone get to the best possible outcome. 
 You care about protecting great brands. Trademarks, brand assets, product names, licensing, co-branding, and enforcement all interest you. You understand how valuable a strong brand can become, and you want to help protect it. And if you’ve got experience in intellectual property law, we’ll probably swoon.
 You’re comfortable in regulated territory. You understand that consumer health businesses operate in a complex regulatory environment. FDA, FTC, advertising law, privacy, disclaimers, licensing, and cross-border requirements don’t intimidate you. Experience in supplements, healthcare, eCommerce, or regulated consumer products would make us especially excited to meet you.

À propos de Taiga 
 Taiga Motors est une entreprise de technologie et de fabrication de véhicules électriques en pleine croissance, chef de file de l’électrification des sports motorisés hors route. Conçus à partir d’une plateforme entièrement nouvelle, nos véhicules offrent un rapport puissance-poids inégalé dans l’industrie ainsi qu’une technologie connectée, sans sacrifier l’environnement.  Le poste 
 À titre de gestionnaire de programme véhicule, vous serez le centre névralgique opérationnel du développement des nouveaux véhicules et mènerez les produits du concept initial jusqu’à un démarrage de production (SOP) réussi. Relevant directement du chef de la direction, vous agirez comme intégrateur de confiance au sein de l’organisation : vous éliminerez les obstacles et veillerez à une exécution irréprochable par les équipes interfonctionnelles.
 Vous serez responsable d’orchestrer l’ensemble du cycle d’introduction de nouveaux produits (NPI). Votre mandat ultime : introduire en usine des changements coordonnés majeurs et de nouvelles plateformes de véhicules dans le respect des délais et des coûts, selon les plus hautes normes de qualité, avec pour objectif un « lancement sans surprise ».
 Principales responsabilités 
 Planification de programme 
 Élaborer et piloter l’échéancier directeur intégré de chaque programme, en reliant les étapes clés de l’ingénierie, de l’outillage, des fournisseurs, de la certification, de la fabrication et du volet commercial aux jalons d’introduction du produit.
 Confirmer avec les chefs de service les livrables, les responsables et les échéances de chaque jalon, et suivre le chemin critique.
 Gérer la portée et les modifications techniques au moyen du processus de gestion des modifications en place, en démontrant leur incidence sur les coûts, les délais et la qualité.
 Exécution interfonctionnelle 
 Animer la réunion hebdomadaire interfonctionnelle du programme et suivre les actions jusqu’à leur clôture.
 Vérifier l’état de préparation aux jalons : confirmer que les livrables de chaque service sont complets avant la revue de jalon et relancer les responsables dès qu’un écart est détecté.
 Animer les revues de jalon et fournir au chef de la direction une recommandation claire de passage ou non (go/no-go), appuyée par des données. Consigner la décision, les risques ouverts et les conditions de passage.
 Résoudre les conflits et les interdépendances entre services; faire remonter les enjeux au chef de la direction, options à l’appui, lorsque des arbitrages exigent une décision.
 Coûts, risques et qualité 
 Suivre les coûts du programme par rapport aux cibles, en collaboration avec les Finances : coût de la nomenclature (BOM), outillage et dépenses en immobilisations, budget de développement et volumes de lancement. Signaler les écarts sans tarder.
 Tenir à jour le registre des risques et des enjeux du programme et piloter les plans d’atténuation avec les services responsables.
 Assurer le suivi de la préparation qualité avec les équipes Qualité et Chaîne d’approvisionnement : actions AMDEC produit et procédé (DFMEA/PFMEA), état de la validation et de la certification, processus d’approbation des pièces de production (PPAP) des fournisseurs et cibles de qualité au lancement.
 Préparation au lancement 
 Piloter le plan de préparation au lancement : montée en cadence de la production, capacité des fournisseurs, préparation du service après-vente (pièces, formation, documentation), déploiement des versions logicielles et calendrier des ventes et du marketing.
 Animer les revues de préparation au lancement et la liste de vérification go/no-go du SOP.
 Diriger les revues post-lancement afin de régler les enjeux en suspens et de documenter le retour d’expérience pour le programme suivant.
 Qualifications et exigences 
 Formation : Baccalauréat ou maîtrise en génie (mécanique, de la production automatisée, industriel ou domaine connexe).
 Expérience : De 5 à 10 ans et plus d’expérience en fabrication complexe, dans l’industrie automobile ou des véhicules électriques, dont au moins 3 ans en gestion directe de programmes NPI, de lancement ou de véhicules.
 Compétences techniques : Capacité démontrée à lire des dessins techniques et des modèles CAO, jumelée à une connaissance approfondie des équipements de fabrication, de l’automatisation et de l’outillage.
 Connaissance des systèmes : Expérience concluante dans l’utilisation et la validation de systèmes d’exécution de la fabrication (MES) et de progiciels de gestion intégrés (ERP).
 Résolution de problèmes : Excellentes habiletés en résolution de problèmes et expérience pratique des outils statistiques et des principes Six Sigma (p. ex., plans d’expériences [DOE], analyse des causes racines) pour optimiser des processus pouvant être déployés à grande échelle.
 Style de leadership : Résilience, flexibilité et aisance face à l’ambiguïté. Grande capacité à influencer sans autorité hiérarchique et à mobiliser les équipes dans un environnement de jeune entreprise au rythme soutenu.
 Ce que nous offrons 
 L’occasion de jouer un rôle fondamental dans l’avenir de l’exploration plein air au sein d’une marque de véhicules électriques de premier plan.
 Une expérience concrète avec les véhicules Taiga : constatez l’impact de votre travail sur le terrain.
 Avantages 
 Environnement dynamique au sein d’une entreprise manufacturière en croissance
 Événements d’entreprise : barbecues, journées de démonstration pour les employés, etc.
 Régime d’assurance collective complet
 REER collectif
 Taiga valorise la diversité dans ses embauches et au sein de son effectif, et accueille les candidatures de personnes de tous horizons, formations et expériences. Nous reconnaissons qu’il existe de nombreux obstacles à l’égalité d’accès à l’emploi et au développement de carrière, et nous nous efforçons d’embaucher des personnes issues de groupes sous-représentés dans l’industrie technologique. Chez Taiga, la diversité signifie favoriser un milieu de travail où les différences sont valorisées pour ce qu’elles apportent à notre équipe.

On the Silicon Enablement Team, you’ll work across architecture, design, verification, firmware, systems, and product to turn ambitious silicon designs into successful products - from early planning and tapeout through board and system bring-up and ongoing support. You’ll build firmware, enablement tests, and reusable engineering infrastructure; investigate real-world failures with automation, instrumentation, and system-level debugging; and translate what you learn into actionable production solutions.  Bring up and debug hardware, investigate failures to actionable root causes, and work across design, verification, firmware, systems, and infrastructure teams to resolve issues and document results.

 Work across the silicon lifecycle, from pre-silicon planning and tapeout through board and system bring-up and ongoing product support.
 Build a broad understanding of how architecture, design, verification, firmware, systems, and product engineering come together to deliver first-silicon success.
 Use firmware, automation, instrumentation, and system-level debugging to understand silicon behavior in real products and turn findings into better designs.
 Contribute to reusable tools and capabilities that enable high-performance computing and support Tenstorrent’s vision for more open computing.

In 1949, as Diners Club tells it, Frank McNamara finished dinner in Manhattan and found his wallet at home in another suit. His wife came down and paid. He returned to the same table the following February and settled the bill with a piece of cardboard, honored at twenty-seven restaurants and carried by two hundred people, most of them his friends. A year later there were 42,000.
 McNamara solved two problems at once. Acceptance: enough restaurants to make the card worth carrying, and enough diners to make it worth accepting. And credit: thirty unsecured days of it, on nothing but a signature. The networks settled acceptance decades ago. What is left is the credit, and the question of why someone carries this card rather than another one. That is this role.
 Mercury is building its first consumer credit card. We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to define what it is, ship it, and grow it from a first cohort into a portfolio. The scope is the credit account itself: the acquisition and application funnel, the approval experience and the underwriting decisions behind it, how the line moves over time, what the rewards are worth, and the experience of carrying the account day to day. 
 Key responsibilities: 
 Build a card people put at the front of the wallet and recommend without being asked
 Take the card from zero to launch: decide what ships first, and carry it through program setup and compliance sign-off
 Make the approval the clearest and fastest in the category: underwriting owns the model, you own the application, the wait, and the answer
 Own how customers experience their line: an increase that feels earned, a decrease that is explained 
 Own the proposition we take to customers, from rewards and redemption to pricing, and understand the economics that fund it
 Set the craft bar: sweat the details, copy, disclosures, latency, empty states, that decide whether a card feels inevitable rather than adequate
 Drive the use of AI where it makes the experience meaningfully better: spend that makes sense at a glance, problems surfaced before they are noticed
 Make correctness and trust product features: own balances, interest, minimum payments, and statements that reconcile, and be measured on them
 Grow the business: own acquisition, activation, retention, and the loops that compound, starting with the businesses Mercury already serves
 Align the ecosystem: bring engineering, design, data, risk, compliance, legal, marketing, support, and partners behind one cohesive plan for the card
 Some things that might make you successful in a role like this: 
 A consumer product manager with taste: you have launched products people chose to use, and can point to the decisions that made them work
 6+ years building consumer products, including at least one where money moved and errors were expensive
 Fluency in credit, or the capacity to acquire it fast: approval rates, line assignment, vintage curves, charge-off, interchange, and rewards liability
 An exceptionally high bar for craft, and a customer-centered, data-driven, and experimentation oriented approach
 You have shipped AI-led products to real consumers and have opinions about what AI makes possible and where it fails
 Exceptional cross-functional collaboration across engineering, design, data, risk, compliance, and partners 
 Sound judgment in a regulated environment: you balance a delightful experience with the controls a credit product requires, and know which corners are never worth cutting
 Nice to have: card issuing, lending, or payments experience, and familiarity with Reg Z and the CARD Act

 Support manufacturing and aftermarket to ensure a smooth transition of new products into production.

We're looking for a Senior Applied Scientist to own the intelligence layer behind our Parts Agent — one of the most strategic bets on our Inventory & EAM roadmap. The agent sits on top of a multi-layer parts data model (PartMaster, StockRecord, PhysicalInstance) and is responsible for answering hard inventory questions: when to reorder, how to optimize stock levels across sites, which parts are at risk of stockout, and how to reconcile messy supplier catalogs into a clean parts master. Your focus will be building the decision models, optimization routines, and AI-powered tools that make those answers trustworthy enough for enterprise maintenance teams to act on.
This is a high-ownership role. You'll shape the modeling approach, partner closely with product and design on what inventory managers actually need, and ship iteratively against feedback from real enterprise customers.

What you'll do

 - Own and evolve the optimization and ML models that power Parts Agent capabilities: reorder point prediction, economic order quantity, multi-site stock balancing, and demand forecasting.

 - Design and implement increasingly sophisticated inventory intelligence: vendor lead time modeling, criticality-weighted safety stock, substitution graph traversal, and proactive stockout alerting.

 - Build and maintain APIs and tools that expose these models to GenAI agent workflows (tool calling, structured input/output), enabling the Parts Agent to take grounded, explainable actions.

 - Partner with PM and design to translate messy real-world inventory problems into tractable models, and push back when "optimal" isn't what operators actually want.

 - Iterate with real users via design partnerships and pilot deployments. Take feedback from parts managers and procurement teams seriously and reflect it back into the model.

 - Contribute to the surrounding Python service: performance, observability, testing, and reliability of the inventory intelligence runtime.

 - Help shape how parts intelligence integrates with the broader MaintainX product over time, including learning from historical usage and purchasing data to continuously improve model inputs.

About you

 - 5+ years of professional software engineering or data science experience, with significant time spent on optimization, forecasting, or ML systems shipped to real users.

 - Strong fluency with at least one optimization paradigm (LP/MILP, stochastic programming, simulation) and practical experience with demand forecasting or inventory management models.

 - Solid Python service engineering: APIs, async, testing, profiling, observability. You can own a production service end-to-end.

 - Academic grounding in Operations Research, Industrial Engineering, Supply Chain, Statistics, or a related quantitative field; strong undergraduate foundation at minimum.

 - Track record of iterating data-driven systems with real users — you've felt what happens when a model recommendation gets rejected and you've redesigned the approach in response.

 - Product mindset and delivery orientation: you ship, you measure, you iterate. You care about the operator outcome, not just the metric.

 - Comfort with ambiguity. You can co-design the data model and feature schema with the team rather than waiting for a clean spec.

 - Familiarity with GenAI tooling (LLM tool calling, structured output, prompt design for constrained generation) is expected.

Nice to have

 - Experience at a known product company shipping inventory management, supply chain, or procurement optimization at scale.

 - Exposure to learning-augmented optimization — using historical purchasing or consumption data to estimate lead times, priors, or constraint weights.

 - Domain experience in MRO (Maintenance, Repair & Operations) inventory, spare parts management, field service logistics, or manufacturing supply chains.

 - Tech-lead experience or interest in growing into a tech-lead role on this team.
